author: T. D. Gregory
title: Golden Acres Living and Rehabilitation Center ranked 3rd in Dallas County nursing home size for Q1 2026
text:
Golden Acres Living and Rehabilitation Center was ranked as the third largest nursing home in Dallas County for the first quarter of 2026, the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) reported .
According to data, the center maintained 264 available beds—132 above the Dallas County quarterly average—and accommodated an average of 173 residents at that time.
The CMS gave Golden Acres Living and Rehabilitation Center an overall rating of 2 out of 5, which trails the Texas state average of 2.7 for nursing homes.
During the first quarter, Five Points at Lake Highlands Nursing and Rehab and Richardson Nursing and Rehabilitation were identified as the largest nursing facilities in Dallas County, each offering 280 beds.
Golden Acres Living and Rehabilitation Center recorded no fines or penalties during this period.
There were a total of 64 for-profit nursing homes throughout Dallas County, Texas.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the population of older adults in the U.S. is increasing, while the number of youth declines. Between 2020 and 2024, the count of Americans age 65 or older rose by 13%, as the population under 18 decreased by 1.7%. Over the last century, the country’s older adult population has surged from 4.9 million in 1920 to beyond 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 study found that almost half of adults in this group—roughly 28 million—may need long-term services and support, and projected that more than a third could ultimately need nursing home care.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
